stories.headline: Google's Gemini 4.0 Pro is 5x cheaper and still hits frontier performance
Top AI voice: treating AI like religion is a real safety risk
Bill Gates wants companies replacing workers with AI to pay a tax
Real estate founder sold his Bentley and is buying 10 Teslas
AI language is officially bleeding into real office meetings

caption:
Here's what happened in AI in the last 24 hours, from Google's cheapest frontier model yet to Bill Gates pushing a robot tax 👇

Google's Gemini 4.0 Pro is 5x cheaper than its previous best and still hits 95% of the same performance, Google just jumped ahead of open-source for the first time.
A top AI voice warned that people treating AI like a god and surrendering their own judgment to it is a genuine safety risk that needs to be taken seriously.
Bill Gates wants companies that replace workers with AI or robots to pay the same payroll taxes a human employee would have generated.
Real estate founder Jason Oppenheim sold his Bentley for a Tesla Model Y, tried FSD once, and is now buying 10 Teslas for his employees.
WSJ says AI's fawning language and "caveman speak" are officially bleeding into real office meetings.

Today's stories point to the same thing: AI is moving fast enough to change how we talk, what cars we drive, who pays taxes, and whether we still trust our own thinking. The people who see this early will have an edge. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: Google, Bill Gates, Wall Street Journal, Tesla, X

pinned_comment: If AI starts to feel more trustworthy than your own doctor or lawyer, where does using a tool end and surrendering your judgment begin? That's the real safety question nobody has a clean answer to yet.
